display: DeepDive knows what's already in your Spotify library, finds the tracks you missed, and turns the music you've saved into mixes built around how you listen.
Dip gives you their best hour, most played first. Dive checks the whole catalogue against your library. Multi-Dip takes a whole bill and builds one playlist in the order they play.
DeepDive's artist chooser showing Dip, Dive and Multi-Dip for Maciann
DeepDive works through every release and shows its progress against the artist image. You can see exactly what it is reading instead of waiting on an unexplained loading screen.
A VIAL dive in progress with the artist photo filling the screen

A Dive reads every album, single and EP, then checks the recordings against your Liked Songs. It catches the same recording under another release instead of trusting titles alone. Review the split, uncheck anything you don't want, then like songs, make a playlist, or both.
A finished Houseghost dive showing duplicate recordings and tracks new to the listener

Your library becomes dozens of useful cuts: years, albums you went deep on, songs you found late, your regulars, and more. Build your own from an era, a length and an artist, or use Sampler to revisit artists you barely touched. Add Last.fm for similar-artist and genre mixes.
DeepDive Mixes showing recommendations, Build your own, Sampler, year, album and listening-history mixes
Put aside artists you mean to get to. Star a few for Up next so Home keeps them in sight, then search, sort and sample everyone else when you're ready.
The Crate with an Up next section and more saved artists below
One playlist for the whole bill
Multi-Dip keeps the artists in show order and fits them to the length of your night. Leave the split even, mark someone More or Less, or give an artist an exact number of songs.
Multi-Dip with Maciann, ValkenWolf and Moonside arranged into a three-hour playlist
There is nowhere for it to go. DeepDive has no server, database or account system—your Spotify library stays in your browser and on your device.
Pick someone you think you know well. That's usually where the surprise is.

Compilations and guest appearances can mean hundreds of extra releases, and Spotify allows only one request at a time — so a prolific artist takes several minutes. Worse, doing this repeatedly can get your Spotify app rate-limited for
, which blocks all searches until it lifts. Use it deliberately rather than routinely, and leave the tab open while it runs.
DeepDive runs on an app of your own, so your listening is never pooled with anyone else's. It's a short form, and you only fill it in once.
It has to match exactly, down to the slash at the end.
It's on your app's page in the dashboard, under Basic Information. You don't need the client secret.
Spotify no longer says what's popular or who sounds like whom. Last.fm does, and with a key you get Dips, Multi-Dips, recommendations and genre mixes.
and copy the API key. It's approved straight away. You can add it later in Settings.

DeepDive makes a cover for each playlist it creates, from the album art inside it. That needs a Spotify permission added after you connected, so it has to be granted once. Everything else works either way.

Every endpoint answered. If a dive still fails, it's the number of requests it makes rather than the endpoints it uses — try a small artist.
Everything is refused with a quota error. This is a limit on your Spotify credentials and only time refills it.
Everything is rate-limited. That's a burst limit rather than a spent budget — wait a minute and run this again before concluding anything.
Some endpoints answer while others are refused, which means the budget is per-group rather than app-wide. The refused ones are the ones to avoid until they recover.
Some endpoints failed without a rate limit — check the status codes above. 403 usually means the endpoint is restricted for this app rather than temporarily unavailable.

Removes those tracks from your Liked Songs. Playlists aren't undone — deleting one you may have edited or shared would be worse than leaving it.
Removing takes the playlist out of your Spotify library. Only playlists DeepDive created are listed — one it merely added to is yours, not ours to remove.

DeepDive knows what's already in your Spotify library, so every playlist it builds is made of the songs you missed.
